title: B1nger--Seeger's 200 Euro Conjecture
statement:
Let $A=(a_{ij})\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ with $n\ge 2$, and let $r_i=(a_{i1},\dots,a_{in})$ denote the $i$th row of $A$. Suppose that

$$
\lVert r_i\rVert_2\ge \sqrt{n-1}\qquad (1\le i\le n).
$$

**B1nger--Seeger's 200 Euro Conjecture.** There exists $x\in\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\{0\}$ such that

$$
|Ax|\ge |x|.
$$

This stronger conjecture was proposed by F. B1nger and A. Seeger in 2024 and is also called the 200 Euro Conjecture. The supplied text does not state that it has been resolved.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.07423

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2026).
source_name: Teng Zhang, “Plank theorems, Gaussian probabilistic estimates and Rump's 100 Euro conjecture”, arXiv:2603.07423 (2026).
